newsitem.title: FRANCE: French employers' chief seen ushering in changes.
newsitem.headline: French employers' chief seen ushering in changes.

text.p: Jean Gandois, chairman of France's employers' federation CNPF, is expected on Tuesday to launch efforts for a major shakeup of the lobby group aimed at modernising the 50-year-old organisation.

"Mr Gandois wants to adapt the organisation to the world of today," a spokeswoman for the Conseil National du Patronat Francais (CNPF) said ahead of the group's annual one-day general meeting in Paris.

The newspaper Le Monde said on Monday that the CNPF was "experiencing a crisis of legitimacy" and that Gandois, the technocratic former head of aluminium group Pechiney who took the CNPF helm two years ago, wanted to shake up the lobby.

A report a year ago by Victor Scherrer, chairman of food group La Vie, suggested that top business chiefs were becoming less involved in employers' groups and that small and medium sized businesses were feeling alienated.
The CNPF is one of France's most influential lobbies and has a big say in the running of France's troubled social security system along with trade unions.
Around a third of faces on the organisation's 35-member executive council could be replaced, paving the way for change, a spokeswoman for the CNPF said in an interview.

One of the key new figures will be Didier Pineau-Valencienne, chairman of electrical engineering group Schneider, who will be in charge of the CNPF's efforts to combat youth unemployment as chairman of its social affairs commission.
"We want to make youth unemployment one of the top priorities. We don't want young people's first taste of the work world to be unemployment," the CNPF spokeswoman said.

A plan for businesses to institute a nine-month apprenticeship diploma programme for young people which would be recognised by the state as an educational qualification is one measure expected to be put forward.
Such a plan might help often prickly relations with the centre-right government which has accused business of not doing enough to reduce France's record 12.6 percent unemployment rate.
President Jacques Chirac criticised companies last year for not hiring more people in response to payroll tax cuts.
Chirac has said better organisation by employers as well as reducing the work week might help.

While the CNPF and the government agree on the need for greater labour market flexibility, the CNPF has been critical of government calls to reduce the work week, saying it would not create more jobs.
